title: Shipped. Weekly, Week of June 08, 2026
og: The week Anthropic put a Mythos-class model in general release, then attached $350 million to what it might cost everyone else. Fable 5, Claude Corps, and the DXC alliance in five days.
dateline: Week of June 08 to June 12, 2026  ///  ISO week 2026-24  ///  Compiled from five daily sweeps
cover_line: Anthropic shipped the most capable model it had ever released to the public, and within forty-eight hours put $350 million behind the argument that the disruption is real.
colophon_line: Shipped. Weekly, ISO week 2026-24. Compiled 2026-08-06 from the daily sweeps of June 08 through June 12, 2026.

paras: Monday the week looked like a distribution story. Apple opened WWDC 2026 with an Extensions framework in iOS 27 that lets a user pick Claude, Gemini, or ChatGPT as the engine behind Siri, Writing Tools, and Image Playground. Gemini holds the native default on a reported $1 billion annual contract. Claude arrives as something you install and then go choose in Settings. Reach, not position.

By Tuesday night that framing was gone. Fable 5 went into general release, not preview, not waitlist, at 80.3% on SWE-Bench Pro against a field whose next best was 69.4%. By Thursday Anthropic had committed $350 million across a nonprofit fellowship and an economic research fund, and Dario Amodei had published tiered policy responses to AI-driven unemployment that run all the way to universal basic income. By Friday DXC Technology had made Fable 5 the default model inside the platform it sells to banks, airlines, insurers, and government agencies.

Capability, conscience, and channel, in that order, in five days. The sequence is the story. A company does not spend $350 million explaining what its product might do to employment unless it believes the product works.

sections.title: The Mythos ceiling came down
paras: [Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-fable-5-mythos-5) landed on June 9 as one release with two doors. Fable 5 is the public model: 80.3% on SWE-Bench Pro, 29.3% on FrontierCode Diamond against 13.4% for Opus 4.8, and spatial reasoning at 38.6% against 14.5%, which is not an improvement so much as a different instrument. Stripe put the practical number on it: a 50-million-line Ruby migration estimated at two-plus months of engineering time finished in a day. Model ID claude-fable-5, 128,000 output tokens, $10 and $50 per million in and out, free on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise through June 22.

Mythos 5 is the same model with some safeguards lifted, distributed through Project Glasswing to authorized cyberdefenders and infrastructure providers. Fable is Mythos with the routing on: roughly one session in twenty touches high-risk territory (cybersecurity, biology) and falls back to Opus 4.8. That is the whole product decision, stated plainly in the release. The public gets the model with a governor. The defenders get it without.

[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/09/anthropic-released-claude-fable-5-its-most-powerful-model-publicly-days-after-warning-ai-is-getting-too-dangerous/) noted that Anthropic shipped its most powerful public model within days of warning that AI is getting too dangerous. Both things are true and they are not in tension: the safeguard routing IS the answer to the warning. Whether one session in twenty is the right number is not a question anyone outside Anthropic can currently check.

Distribution followed the same day. [GitHub Copilot](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-06-09-claude-fable-5-is-generally-available-for-github-copilot/) made Fable 5 selectable for subscribers. [Amazon Bedrock](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/anthropic-claude-fable-5-on-aws-mythos-class-capabilities-with-built-in-safeguards-now-available/) carried it at launch, with Vertex and Foundry to follow. Nine SDK releases went out across Python and TypeScript to add the model identifiers, server-side refusal fallbacks, and a client-side fallback middleware for providers that do not support them.

sections.title: $350 million is a number you say out loud on purpose
paras: On June 10 Anthropic committed $200 million to an [Economic Futures Research Fund](https://www.anthropic.com/research/economic-policy-responses) and published a Dario Amodei policy essay proposing tiered government responses to AI-driven unemployment at 5%, 10%, and beyond, escalating to universal basic income and equity-sharing frameworks. The same package proposed an Advanced AI Framework with mandatory testing, independent evaluation, and civil penalties tied to global revenue for developers training above 10^25 FLOPs.

On June 11 came [Claude Corps](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-corps): $150 million placing 1,000 early-career workers inside US nonprofits for a year at $85,000 each, trained on Claude, run with CodePath and Social Finance, with more than 400 nonprofits hosting in year one. No degree required. Over 18, under two years of full-time experience, authorized to work in the US. First cohort of 100 starts October 19.

The read: this is the first time Anthropic has attached a dollar figure to economic mitigation alongside its capability agenda, and it did it in the same week it removed the ceiling on that agenda. A company proposing civil penalties tied to its own revenue, on a threshold its own models cross, is not lobbying for looser rules. It is trying to write the rules while it still has standing to.

entries.title: Apple WWDC 2026: iOS 27 Extensions bring Claude to Siri
entries.body: An Extensions framework lets users designate Claude, Gemini, or ChatGPT as the AI model behind Siri, Writing Tools, and Image Playground. Gemini is the native default on a reported $1 billion annual Apple to Google contract; Claude arrives as a user-installed extension selected in Settings under Apple Intelligence. iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27 ship fall 2026. No Anthropic press release accompanied it.

entries.title: Claude for Apple Foundation Models framework
entries.body: A Swift package making Claude available as a server-side language model inside Apple's Foundation Models framework, conforming to the LanguageModel protocol so it can be driven with LanguageModelSession alongside Apple's on-device model. Multi-step reasoning, code generation, web search, code execution, SwiftUI streaming. Announced June 9, available June 10.

entries.title: Managed Agents: cron schedules and credential vaults, public beta
entries.body: Agents can be attached to a cron schedule on the Claude Platform and fire without a manual trigger. Credential vault integration keeps secrets out of model context entirely, binding keys at the network boundary only for requests to customer-allowlisted domains. No separate scheduler fee. Reported by itbrief.news.

entries.title: DXC Technology multi-year global alliance
entries.body: DXC tested Claude across its 115,000-person workforce in 70 countries before rolling it to clients. Claude wrote more than 95% of the code for DXC OASIS, its AI-native orchestration platform, with Fable 5 as the default foundation model. DXC is training tens of thousands of Claude-certified forward-deployed engineers to install Claude inside the systems regulated industries have run for decades. Not a product launch: an established firm putting Claude at the center of what it sells.

sections.title: Claude Code, five days, seven versions

entries.title: v2.1.175 and v2.1.174
entries.body: v2.1.175 adds the enforceAvailableModels managed setting: when enabled, the availableModels allowlist also governs what Default resolves to, closing the gap organizations kept finding. v2.1.174 adds wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled and fixes the /model picker hiding the family Default resolves to.

entries.title: v2.1.173
entries.body: Fable 5 model names carrying a [1m] suffix are now normalized automatically, since Fable 5 ships with 1M context by default and the suffix was causing match failures. Fixed a spurious sandbox-dependencies-missing warning on Windows. Thinking summaries in collapsed groups render as markdown, hold for at least 3 seconds, and cap at 10 lines.

entries.title: v2.1.172
entries.body: Sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents, up to 5 levels deep, on by default. Bedrock reads the AWS region from ~/.aws when AWS_REGION is unset, matching AWS SDK precedence. Search bar in the plugin marketplace. Fixed sessions using 1M context without usage credits getting permanently stuck: they now auto-compact under the standard limit.

entries.title: v2.1.170 and v2.1.169
entries.body: v2.1.170 adds Fable 5 access and fixes transcript saving for sessions launched from the VS Code integrated terminal. v2.1.169 adds --safe-mode (and CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE) to disable all customizations for clean troubleshooting, /cd to move a session without breaking the prompt cache, and disableBundledSkills. Ten bug fixes across enterprise MCP policy, Windows startup, and remote reattachment.

entries.title: Nine SDK releases across Python and TypeScript
entries.body: Python v0.108.0 and TypeScript v0.103.0 add the claude-fable-5 and claude-mythos-5 identifiers, server-side refusal fallbacks, and client-side fallback middleware. v0.109.0 and v0.104.0 add Managed Agents deployments and environment variable credentials. v0.109.1 and v0.104.1 add the frontier_llm refusal category. Platform SDKs vertex v0.17.1, foundry v0.3.1, bedrock v0.30.2, and aws v0.4.2 all fixed third-party middleware ordering within 60 seconds of each other.

entries.title: anthropic-sdk-python v0.107.1
entries.body: One bug fix carried into Monday's window: the Foundry client was not sending the x-api-key header for API-key authentication.

paras: One deprecation sat under the whole week. claude-sonnet-4-20250514 and claude-opus-4-20250514 retired on June 15, three days after this week closed. Anything pinning either identifier began returning errors that Sunday. The migration targets were claude-sonnet-4-6 and claude-opus-4-7, and the notice ran in Wednesday's sweep with five days on the clock.

Worth noting what a retired model identifier actually costs, since it is easy to read a deprecation line as housekeeping. It returns 404 not_found, not 401. Anything watching for an auth failure sees a healthy credential and a missing target, and looks in the wrong place.

close: Anthropic spent this week proving it can build the thing and arguing about what the thing will cost. The interesting part is that it did both at full volume, in public, four days apart.
